title: ASCOD Algorithm pour Ischemic AVC
formula:
Grades of predefined ASCOD phenotypes:

| Finding | ASCOD Grade |
| --- | --- |
| Workup is insufficient to grade the disease | 9 |
| Disease is present and potentially a cause | 1 |
| Disease is present but causal link is uncertain | 2 |
| Disease is present but causal link is unlikely | 3 |
| Disease is absent | 0 |

Specific definitions:

| A: Causality grades for atherothrombosis | |
| --- | --- |
| A9: Incomplete workup | Ultrasound (Duplex or TCD), angiogram (CTA, MRA, or conventional), or autopsy not performed (a minimum workup is extra- and intracranial assessment of cerebral arteries - maximum workup also includes transesophageal assessment of the aortic arch (or a default CTA of the aortic arch)) |
| A1: Potentially causal (atherothrombotic stroke) | 50-99% ipsilateral atherosclerotic stenosis in intra/extracranial artery supplying the ischemic field |
| Ipsilateral atherosclerotic stenosis <50% in intra/extracranial artery with endoluminal thrombus supplying ischemic field | |
| Mobile thrombus in aortic arch | |
| Ipsilateral arterial occlusion in intra/extracranial artery with evidence of underlying atherosclerotic plaque supplying ischemic field | |
| A2: Causal link uncertain | 30-50% ipsilateral atherosclerotic stenosis in intra/extracranial artery supplying the ischemic field |
| Aortic plaque ≥4 mm without mobile lesion | |
| A3: Causal link unlikely but disease is present | <30% stenosis in intra/extracranial artery ipsilateral to infarct area |
| Aortic plaque <4 mm without mobile thrombus | |
| Stenosis (any degree) or occlusion in a cerebral artery not supplying infarct area (e.g. contralateral side, opposite circulation) | |
| History of MI, coronary revascularization, or peripheral arterial disease | |
| 50-99% ipsi/bilateral atherosclerotic stenosis with bihemispheric MR-DWI lesion | |
| A0: Atherosclerosis not detected and ruled out | Any of the following done and negative for extracranial arterial stenosis: duplex US, CTA, MRA, conventional angiogram, or autopsy |
| Any of the following done and negative for intracranial arterial stenosis: transcranial Doppler US, MRA, CTA, conventional angiogram, or autopsy | |
| TEE with specific assessment of the aortic arch (when the probe is pulled back at end of cardiac examination, turn probe counterclockwise and watch aortic arch), or specific aortic arch assessment with CTA to rule out aortic arch atheroma | |

| S: Causality grades for small-vessel disease | |
| --- | --- |
| S9: Incomplete workup | MRI or CT not done |
| S1: Potentially causal | Lacunar infarction, defined as small deep infarct <15 mm in perforator branch territory on MRI-DWI or default CT in area corresponding to symptoms, plus ≥1 of the following: |
| ≥1 small deep older infarct(s) of lacunar type in other territories | |
| Severe (confluent/Fazekas III) leukoaraiosis, or microbleeds, or severe dilatation of perivascular spaces (‘état criblé’) | |
| Repeated, recent (<1 month), TIAs attributable to the same territory as the index infarct | |
| S2: Causal link uncertain | Only one recent lacunar infarction and no other abnormality on MRI/CT |
| Clinical syndrome suggestive of deep branch artery stroke, without ischemic lesion in appropriate area on MRI/CT (main clinical syndrome suggesting a deep branch artery/lacunar stroke: pure hemiparesis, pure hemisensory loss, ataxic hemiparesis, dysarthria-clumsy hand syndrome, unilateral sensorimotor deficit, others: hemichorea, hemiballism, pure dysarthria, etc) | |
| S3: Causal link unlikely, but disease is present | Severe (confluent/Fazekas III) leukoaraiosis visible on MRI and/or CT scan, and/or microbleeds visible on T2-weighted MRI, and/or severe dilatation of perivascular spaces (visible on T2-weighted MRI), and/or one or several old, small deep infarcts of lacunar type |
| S0: Small-vessel disease not detected | Negative MRI (T2, FLAIR, GRE, DWI) and no clinical syndrome suggestive of deep branch artery stroke |

| C: Causality grades for cardiac pathology | |
| --- | --- |
| C9: Incomplete workup | Minimum is EKG and examination by trained cardiologist in absence of cardiac imaging |
| C1: Potentially causal | Acute cardiogenic stroke, or recent stroke and older bihemispheric, supra/infratentorial territorial, or cortical ischemic lesions and signs of systemic embolism with ≥1 of the following: |
| Mitral stenosis (surface area <1.5 cm²) | |
| Mechanical valve | |
| MI within 4 weeks before stroke | |
| Mural thrombus in the left cavities | |
| Left ventricular aneurysm | |
| History or presence of documented afib (paroxysmal (>60 seconds), persistent, or permanent) or flutter, with or without left atrial thrombus or spontaneous echo | |
| Atrial disease (tachy-brady syndrome) | |
| Dilated or hypertrophic cardiomyopathies | |
| Left ventricle ejection fraction <35% | |
| Endocarditis | |
| Intracardiac mass | |
| PFO and thrombus in situ | |
| PFO and concomitant PE or proximal DVT preceding the index stroke | |
| Aforementioned cardiac pathologies (C1) with single or without obvious cerebral ischemic lesion | |
| C2: Causal link is uncertain (one of the following, regardless of stroke pattern) | PFO and atrial septal aneurysm |
| PFO and PE or proximal DTV concomitant but NOT preceding the index stroke | |
| Intracardiac spontaneous echo-contrast | |
| Apical akinesia of the left ventricle and decreased ejection fraction (but >35%) | |
| History of MI or palpitation and multiple brain infarction, repeated either bilateral or in two different arterial territories (e.g. both anterior and posterior circulation) | |
| No direct cardiac source identified, but multiple brain infarction, repeated either bilateral or in two different arterial territories (e.g. both anterior and posterior circulation) and/or evidence of systemic emboli: renal or splenic or mesenteric infarction (on CT, MRI, or autopsy) or embolism in peripheral artery supplying arm or leg | |
| C3: Causal link unlikely but disease is present (one of the following abnormalities present in isolation) | PFO, ASA , strands, mitral annulus calcification, aortic valve calcification, nonapical akinesia of left ventricle, transient afib <60 sec, or atrial hyperexcitability |
| C0: Cardiac pathology not detected or not suspected | Ruling out a cardiac source of embolism: minimum is negative EKG and examination by a cardiologist; maximum is negative EKG/telemetry/24-hour Holter EKG/long-term EKG recording (implantable device, transtelephonic EKG, loop recorder), negative TEE for atrium, valves, and septal abnormalities, negative TTE for PFO and assessment of left ventricle, negative cardiac CT/MRI, and negative abdominal CT/MRI (search for old or simultaneous subdiaphragmatic visceral infarction) |

| O: Causality for other causes | |
| --- | --- |
| O9: Incomplete workup | Unable to reasonably exclude other causes based on best available diagnostic tests and stroke-specific history |
| O1: Potentially causal | Dolichoectasia with complicated aneurysm |
| Polycythemia vera or thrombocythemia >800,000/mm³ | |
| Systemic lupus | |
| Disseminated intravascular coagulation | |
| Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome (including >100 GPL units or lupus anticoagulant) | |
| Fabry’s disease | |
| Coexisting meningitis | |
| Sickle cell disease | |
| Ruptured intracranial aneurysm with or without vasospasm of the artery supplying the infarcted area | |
| Severe hyperhomocysteinemia | |
| Horton’s disease | |
| Other cerebral inflammatory or infectious angiitis | |
| Moyamoya disease, etc. | |
| O2: Causal link is uncertain | Saccular aneurysm (with suspicion of embolism) |
| Coincidental migraine attack with neurological deficit lasting >60 min in patients with history of migraine aura | |
| O3: Causal link is unlikely but disease is present | Arteriovenous malformation |
| Thrombocytosis <800,000/mm³ | |
| Antiphospholipid antibody <100 GPL units | |
| Homocysteinemia <40 μmol/L | |
| Malignoma with associated hypercoagulation (high D-dimer levels), DVT/PE and/or recent chemotherapy | |
| O0: Cardiac pathology not detected or not suspected | Ruling out other causes: negative: CSF , complete hemostasis, cerebral arterial imaging, family history of inherited disease, inflammatory markers ( ESR and CRP ), hematologic tests (platelet, leukocytes, and eosinophilic counts; hematocrit), specific tests according to suspected disease (e.g. genetic test, retinal angiography for Susac syndrome) |

| D: Causality grades for dissection | |
| --- | --- |
| D9: Incomplete workup | In patients <60 years old and no evidence of A1, A2, S1, C1, or O1 category: no fat-saturated MRI performed on the extra/intracranial artery supplying the ischemic field or no x-ray angiography performed (all performed within 15 days of symptom onset) |
| D1: Potentially causal | Arterial dissection by direct demonstration (evidence of mural hematoma: hypersignal on fat-saturated MRI or at autopsy or on TOF-MRA or CT on axial sections showing both enlargement of the arterial wall by the hematoma with narrowing of the lumen or on echography showing an hypoechoic arterial wall with narrowing of the lumen and sudden enlargement of the carotid or vertebral (V2) artery diameter |
| Arterial dissection by indirect demonstration or by less sensitive/less specific diagnostic test (only long arterial stenosis beyond carotid bifurcation or in V2, V3, or V4 without demonstration of arterial wall hematoma: on x-ray angiography, and/or echography and/or CTA and/or MRA) or unequivocal US with recanalization during follow-up | |
| D2: Causal link uncertain | Arterial dissection by weak evidence (suggestive clinical history, e.g. painful Horner’s syndrome or past history of arterial dissection) |
| Imaging evidence of fibromuscular dysplasia of a cerebral artery supplying ischemic field | |
| D3: Causal link unlikely but disease is present | Kinking or dolichoectasia without complicated aneurysm or plicature |
| Fibromuscular dysplasia on arteries not supplying ischemic field | |
| D0: No dissection detected or suspected | Ruling out dissection: negative fat-saturated MRI of suspected artery or good quality, normal x-ray angiography (too early fat-saturated MRI performed within three days of symptom onset can be falsely negative and then should be repeated). If no clinical suspicion of dissection, patient can be classified D0 provided good-quality extra/intracranial cerebral artery and cardiac evaluations have been done |

how_to_use.why:
- Peut aider à une évaluation complète du bilan diagnostique et des constatations afin de rendre compte de tous les mécanismes pathologiques sous-jacents présents chez les patients atteints d’AVC ischémique, permettant ainsi potentiellement de guider la prise en charge des facteurs de risque pour la prévention secondaire.
- Par rapport à TOAST, réduit la proportion d’AVC classés « d’étiologie indéterminée » malgré un bilan approfondi ([Radu 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030384671730149X)).
how_to_use.when: À utiliser chez les patients pour une évaluation exhaustive de toutes les causes sous-jacentes potentielles d’AVC ischémique, ce qui peut aider chez ceux dont l’étiologie est incertaine ou intriquée.
how_to_use.pearls: - Le phénotypage ASCOD de l'AVC ischémique vise à attribuer un degré de probabilité de relation causale à chaque mécanisme pathologique sous-jacent potentiel, sans pondérer en faveur de la cause la plus probable. next_steps.advice:
- Un bilan minimal incomplet peut amener à réaliser des examens diagnostiques supplémentaires listés dans les critères du score.
- Les mécanismes pathologiques potentiellement causaux doivent être traités selon les recommandations actuelles fondées sur les preuves pour la prévention secondaire de l’AVC.
- Lorsque plusieurs mécanismes pathologiques potentiellement causaux coexistent, ils doivent tous être pris en compte pour le traitement.
next_steps.critical_actions: L'ASCOD traite des mécanismes sous-jacents de l'AVC ischémique, et non de tous les aspects des soins post-AVC, qui peuvent inclure la rééducation, la physiothérapie, l'ergothérapie et l'orthophonie.
next_steps.management: La prise en charge dépend du ou des mécanismes identifiés et peut inclure une anticoagulation, des anti-thrombotiques, des hypolipémiants à haute intensité, un contrôle de la pression artérielle et de la glycémie, une endartériectomie carotidienne et/ou une réparation d'une communication interauriculaire.

evidence:
- Ischemic stroke without clear etiology has historically been difficult to define and classify. In 2009, a new system for phenotyping patients called ASCO (A for atherosclerosis; S for small-vessel disease, C for cardiac pathology, and O for other causes) was proposed by expert consensus in order to better describe the overlap between multiple potential causative diseases underlying ischemic stroke ([Amarenco 2009](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/19342826)).
- ASCO was subsequently updated to include dissection (D), a common cause of stroke in young patients ([Amarenco 2013](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/23899749)).
- About 90% of ischemic stroke patients identified with ASCOD have atherosclerotic disease, highlighting importance of risk factor control regardless of most causal mechanism for index stroke. These patients have high overlap between multiple possible ischemic stroke etiologies ([Sirimarco 2013](https://stroke.ahajournals.org/content/44/9/2427)).
- Reported interrater agreement for ASCOD classification is substantial: kappa 0.95 for large vessel atherosclerosis, 0.95 for small vessel disease, and 1 for cardiac disease, which outscores TOAST ([Radu 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030384671730149X)).
- Some comparisons among proposed classification systems including TOAST, Causative Classification of Stroke (CCS) system, and ASCO show good overall agreement between all classification systems ([Radu 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030384671730149X)).
- A recent study comparing TOAST, CCS, and ASCO finds that all systems generated etiologic subtypes with different 90-day stroke recurrence, 90-day survival, admission stroke severity, and acute infarct burden, with CCS providing the greatest discrimination in all outcomes except 90-day survival. This suggests CCS may be more suitable in etiologic subtype assessment in large stroke clinical trials ([Arsava 2017](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3013495/)).
medium_description: Assigns phenotype chez les patients avec ischemic AVC de uncertain causes.

input_schema.name: a9
input_schema.label: 9 : Bilan incomplet
input_schema.tips: Ultrasound (Duplex or TCD), angiogram (CTA, MRA, or conventional), or autopsy not performed (a minimum workup is extra- and intracranial assessment of cerebral arteries - maximum workup also includes transesophageal assessment of the aortic arch (or a default CTA of the aortic arch))

input_schema.name: a1
input_schema.label: 1 : Potentiellement causal (AVC athérothrombotique)
input_schema.tips: 50-99% ipsilateral atherosclerotic stenosis in intra/extracranial artery supplying the ischemic field, ipsilateral atherosclerotic stenosis <50% in intra/extracranial artery with endoluminal thrombus supplying ischemic field, mobile thrombus in aortic arch, ipsilateral arterial occlusion in intra/extracranial artery with evidence of underlying atherosclerotic plaque supplying ischemic field

input_schema.name: a2
input_schema.label: 2 : Lien de causalité incertain
input_schema.tips: Sténose athéroscléreuse ipsilatérale de 30-50 % d'une artère intracrânienne ou extracrânienne irriguant le territoire ischémique, plaque aortique ≥4 mm sans lésion mobile

input_schema.name: a3
input_schema.label: 3 : Lien de causalité improbable, mais la maladie est présente
input_schema.tips: 30% stenosis in intra/extracranial artery ipsilateral to infarct area, aortic plaque <4 mm without mobile thrombus, stenosis (any degree) or occlusion in a cerebral artery not supplying infarct area (e.g. contralateral side, opposite circulation), history of MI, coronary revascularization, or peripheral arterial disease, 50-99% ipsi/bilateral atherosclerotic stenosis with bihemispheric magnetic resonance-diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) lesion

input_schema.name: a0
input_schema.label: 0 : Athérosclérose non détectée et écartée
input_schema.tips: Any of the following done and negative for extracranial arterial stenosis: duplex US, CTA, MRA, conventional angiogram, or autopsy; any of the following done and negative for intracranial arterial stenosis: transcranial Doppler US, MRA, CTA, conventional angiogram, or autopsy; transesophageal echocardiography with specific assessment of the aortic arch (when the probe is pulled back at end of cardiac examination, turn probe counterclockwise and watch aortic arch), or specific aortic arch assessment with CTA to rule out aortic arch atheroma

input_schema.name: s9
input_schema.label: S9 : Bilan incomplet
input_schema.tips: IRM ou TDM non réalisés

input_schema.name: s1
input_schema.label: S1 : Potentiellement causal
input_schema.tips: Lacunar infarction, defined as small deep infarct <15 mm in perforator branch territory on MRI-DWI or default CT in area corresponding to symptoms, plus ≥1 of the following: ≥1 small deep older infarct(s) of lacunar type in other territories; severe (confluent/Fazekas III) leukoaraiosis, or microbleeds, or severe dilatation of perivascular spaces (‘état criblé’); repeated, recent (<1 month), TIAs attributable to the same territory as the index infarct

input_schema.name: s2
input_schema.label: S2 : Lien causal incertain
input_schema.tips: Only one recent lacunar infarction and no other abnormality on MRI/CT, clinical syndrome suggestive of deep branch artery stroke, without ischemic lesion in appropriate area on MRI/CT (main clinical syndrome suggesting a deep branch artery/lacunar stroke: pure hemiparesis, pure hemisensory loss, ataxic hemiparesis, dysarthria-clumsy hand syndrome, unilateral sensorimotor deficit, others: hemichorea, hemiballism, pure dysarthria, etc)

input_schema.name: s3
input_schema.label: S3 : Lien causal peu probable, mais la maladie est présente
input_schema.tips: Severe (confluent/Fazekas III) leukoaraiosis visible on MRI and/or CT scan, and/or microbleeds visible on T2-weighted MRI, and/or severe dilatation of perivascular spaces (visible on T2-weighted MRI), and/or one or several old, small deep infarcts of lacunar type

input_schema.name: s0
input_schema.label: S0 : Maladie des petits vaisseaux non détectée
input_schema.tips: IRM négative (T2, FLAIR, GRE, DWI) et aucun syndrome clinique évocateur d'un infarctus des artères de branches profondes

input_schema.name: c9
input_schema.label: C9 : Bilan incomplet
input_schema.tips: Minimum : EKG et examen par un cardiologue formé en l’absence d’imagerie cardiaque

input_schema.name: c1
input_schema.label: C1 : Potentiellement causal
input_schema.tips: Acute cardiogenic stroke, or recent stroke and older bihemispheric, supra/infratentorial territorial, or cortical ischemic lesions and signs of systemic embolism with ≥1 of the following: mitral stenosis (surface area <1.5 cm²), mechanical valve, MI within 4 weeks before stroke mural thrombus in the left cavities, left ventricular aneurysm, history or presence of documented afib (paroxysmal (>60 seconds), persistent, or permanent) or flutter, with or without left atrial thrombus or spontaneous echo, atrial disease (tachy-brady syndrome), dilated or hypertrophic cardiomyopathies, left ventricle ejection fraction <35%, endocarditis, intracardiac mass, patent foramen ovale (PFO) and thrombus in situ, PFO and concomitant PE or proximal DVT preceding the index stroke, aforementioned cardiac pathologies (C1) with single or without obvious cerebral ischemic lesion

input_schema.name: c2
input_schema.label: C2: Causal link is uncertain (one de following, regardless de AVC pattern)
input_schema.tips: PFO and atrial septal aneurysm, PFO and PE or proximal DTV concomitant but NOT preceding the index stroke, intracardiac spontaneous echo-contrast, apical akinesia of the left ventricle and decreased ejection fraction (but >35%), history of MI or palpitation and multiple brain infarction, repeated either bilateral or in two different arterial territories (e.g. both anterior and posterior circulation), no direct cardiac source identified, but multiple brain infarction, repeated either bilateral or in two different arterial territories (e.g. both anterior and posterior circulation) and/or evidence of systemic emboli: renal or splenic or mesenteric infarction (on CT, MRI, or autopsy) or embolism in peripheral artery supplying arm or leg

input_schema.name: c3
input_schema.label: C3: Causal link unlikely but maladie is present (one de following abnormalities present dans isolation)
input_schema.tips: PFO, atrial septal aneurysm (ASA), strands, mitral annulus calcification, aortic valve calcification, nonapical akinesia of left ventricle, transient afib <60 sec, or atrial hyperexcitability

input_schema.name: c0
input_schema.label: C0 : pathologie cardiaque non détectée ou non suspectée
input_schema.tips: Ruling out a cardiac source of embolism: minimum is negative EKG and examination by a cardiologist; maximum is negative EKG/telemetry/24-hour Holter EKG/long-term EKG recording (implantable device, transtelephonic EKG, loop recorder), negative TEE for atrium, valves, and septal abnormalities, negative transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) for PFO and assessment of left ventricle, negative cardiac CT/MRI, and negative abdominal CT/MRI (search for old or simultaneous subdiaphragmatic visceral infarction)

input_schema.name: o9
input_schema.label: O9 : Bilan incomplet
input_schema.tips: Incapable d’exclure raisonnablement d’autres causes sur la base des meilleurs examens diagnostiques disponibles et de l’anamnèse spécifique à l’AVC

input_schema.name: o1
input_schema.label: O1 : Potentiellement causal
input_schema.tips: Dolichoectasia with complicated aneurysm, polycythemia vera or thrombocythemia >800,000/mm³, systemic lupus, disseminated intravascular coagulation, antiphospholipid antibody syndrome (including >100 IgG antiphospholipid (GPL) units or lupus anticoagulant), Fabry’s disease, coexisting meningitis, sickle cell disease, ruptured intracranial aneurysm with or without vasospasm of the artery supplying the infarcted area, severe hyperhomocysteinemia, Horton’s disease, other cerebral inflammatory or infectious angiitis, Moyamoya disease, etc.

input_schema.name: o2
input_schema.label: O2 : Lien de causalité incertain
input_schema.tips: Saccular aneurysm (with suspicion of embolism), coincidental migraine attack with neurological deficit lasting >60 min in patients with history of migraine aura

input_schema.name: o3
input_schema.label: O3 : Lien de causalité peu probable, mais la maladie est présente
input_schema.tips: Arteriovenous malformation, thrombocytosis <800,000/mm³ antiphospholipid antibody <100 GPL units, homocysteinemia <40 μmol/L, malignoma with associated hypercoagulation (high D-dimer levels), DVT/PE and/or recent chemotherapy

input_schema.name: o0
input_schema.label: O0 : Pathologie cardiaque non détectée ou non suspectée
input_schema.tips: Ruling out other causes: negative Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), complete hemostasis, cerebral arterial imaging, family history of inherited disease, inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP)), hematologic tests (platelet, leukocytes, and eosinophilic counts; hematocrit), specific tests according to suspected disease (e.g. genetic test, retinal angiography for Susac syndrome)

input_schema.name: d9
input_schema.label: D9 : Bilan incomplet
input_schema.tips: In patients <60 years old and no evidence of A1, A2, S1, C1, or O1 category: no fat-saturated MRI performed on the extra/intracranial artery supplying the ischemic field or no x-ray angiography performed (all performed within 15 days of symptom onset)

input_schema.name: d1
input_schema.label: D1 : Potentiellement causal
input_schema.tips: Arterial dissection by direct demonstration (evidence of mural hematoma: hypersignal on fat-saturated MRI or at autopsy or on TOF-MRA or CT on axial sections showing both enlargement of the arterial wall by the hematoma with narrowing of the lumen or on echography showing an hypoechoic arterial wall with narrowing of the lumen and sudden enlargement of the carotid or vertebral (V2) artery diameter, arterial dissection by indirect demonstration or by less sensitive/less specific diagnostic test (only long arterial stenosis beyond carotid bifurcation or in V2, V3, or V4 without demonstration of arterial wall hematoma: on x-ray angiography, and/or echography and/or CTA and/or MRA) or unequivocal US with recanalization during follow-up

input_schema.name: d2
input_schema.label: D2 : Lien de causalité incertain
input_schema.tips: Dissection artérielle sur arguments faibles (histoire clinique évocatrice, p. ex. syndrome de Horner douloureux ou antécédent de dissection artérielle), signes d’imagerie de dysplasie fibromusculaire d’une artère cérébrale irriguant le territoire ischémique

input_schema.name: d3
input_schema.label: D3 : lien de causalité peu probable, mais la maladie est présente.
input_schema.tips: Kinking ou dolichoectasie sans anévrisme compliqué ni plicature, dysplasie fibromusculaire sur des artères ne vascularisant pas le territoire ischémique

input_schema.name: d0
input_schema.label: D0 : Aucune dissection détectée ou suspectée
input_schema.tips: Exclusion d’une dissection : IRM avec saturation de graisse négative de l’artère suspectée ou angiographie par rayons X normale et de bonne qualité (une IRM avec saturation de graisse réalisée trop précocement, dans les trois jours suivant le début des symptômes, peut être faussement négative et doit alors être répétée). En l’absence de suspicion clinique de dissection, le patient peut être classé D0 à condition que des évaluations de bonne qualité des artères cérébrales extra/intracrâniennes et cardiaques aient été réalisées.
